steps.observation: GATE2-EVIDENCE-0903 (2026-09-03). The other half of the owner's 'give revives after the tournament' instruction, and the defect the revives alone uncovered. S05-09a deploys the active creature immediately after the load -- BEFORE this recovery block -- and at that moment the active creature is Moss, brought out of the tournament final on 0/142.8 HP. A fainted creature cannot be sent out, so no ally body was ever created; reviving Moss a few steps later restores the creature but nothing re-deploys it. `encounter_director.gd::can_challenge()` requires `_ally_body != null and is_instance_valid(_ally_body)`, so with a fully healthy five-creature party (nobody fainted, 38-113 HP each) BOTH of this segment's fights refused to start: Old Bram at (195,905) and the South Bridge grunt at (14,1314) each answered with `no_usable_ally()`'s line -- 'Your creature can't fight like this... a bed will do it, or something to eat' / 'Come find me again once you've got something to send out.' -- `combat_running=false`, and `south_bridge_open` was never set, so the chapter's own physical gate could not be earned. Measured on run S05-superseded-4 (98P/7F): every downstream failure in it descends from this one press. Sending the creature back out is what a player does after reviving it.

steps._comment_route: RIG-F6, ralph/GATE-F-FULL 2026-08-30. S05-19 walked straight from the tournament ground to (-40,180) and the straight line crosses the village outline at (16.6, 21.5), 37.6 m from the nearest gate. `data/config/village_boundary.json` gave the village a closed fence on 2026-08-30 (OP-0830-1, then the straddle fix the same day) and `village_boundary.gd` builds it as sealed StaticBody3D panels with a hole only at each gate, so the walk hit a wall: measured, `did not reach (-40, 180) in 11700 walking frames; stopped 155.8 m short at (-15.0, 1.0, 26.0)` -- which is the outline's own [-15,27] vertex, 22 m from PondGate. The next walk then failed identically from the same spot, and every walk after it would have. NOT A GAME DEFECT: `road_gate_open` is set from S02 and `village_boundary.gd` swings BOTH gates on that flag, so a player following the Pond road out of the village leaves freely -- `terrain_playground.json`'s third route is exactly (10,-10) -> (-14,14) -> (-45,45) -> (-105,115), through PondGate at (-21,21). This segment predates the fence and was still walking as though the village had no edge. Split into three legs that follow the road the player follows: to the gate, through it, then on to the spine. Checked against the outline before authoring -- the only crossing on the three legs is the gate itself.

steps.expected: GATE-F-LEG-S05 fix, second measurement. Winning the trainer does NOT open the gate by itself -- `_on_tried()` (the gate's own physical Interactable, `prompt_label(): "Try the bridge gate"`) is the only caller of `item_gate.gd::try_open()`, which is the only thing that consumes `south_bridge_key` and sets `south_bridge_open`; `_pay_trainer_reward` grants the key to the satchel on defeat but nothing about the fight ending touches the gate. The first fix (this step against (0,1330)) reached its literal target -- but data/config/terrain_playground.json's own `crossings[].south_bridge.carve.centre` is `[8, 1330]`, not `[0,1330]`, and the leaf itself stands `bridge.gate_offset` (8.5m) back toward the village along the crossing's axis, at `[8, 1321.5]` (matches south_bridge_grunt's own `_why_here`: '9.6m from the locked leaf at [8, 1321.5]'). (0,1330) is 11.7m from the actual leaf -- outside its 4.0m interact radius -- and OW5C's own comment names x=0 as sitting exactly on a known, separately-tracked collision-shape-tile seam (COLL1, docs/CURRENT_STATE.md Phase -1.40) that a walk glued to a fixed x can get stuck crossing; the run that found this saw exactly that (severed_spokes recovery firing repeatedly, an erratic path, and a false 'reached' report from a recovery point nowhere near the leaf). (8, 1319) sits on the seam-safe x the crossing's own road was already moved to (OW5C) and 2.5m short of the leaf on the near side, inside the interact radius without walking through it.

With the key already in the satchel from the trainer's reward, `_on_tried()` calls `try_open()`, which consumes it and sets `south_bridge_open`; `_unlock()` swings the leaf and disables its collider and its own prompt.

steps.title: let the gate open
steps.expected: the unlock is an instant re-pose (gated_crossing.gd::_unlock has no tween on the leaf itself, unlike the locked jar), but the flag write and the collider disable go through the same frame the interact resolves on; this settles it before the assert below reads it

steps.title: the South Bridge is open
steps.expected: `south_bridge_open` closes section E.5 objective 16/27

steps.title: the world owns input before this walk
steps.expected: no narrative modal is holding locomotion when this walk starts
steps.observation: T2-GATEF-RUN6 modal-holds-locomotion audit. A walk that begins while a narrative modal still owns input does not fail as 'a modal is open' -- it fails as 'did not reach', many steps and sometimes many minutes later, which is how X04 lost its whole combat block to 3601 held frames. This assert is diagnostic and changes no behaviour: it turns that silent cascade into one named cause at the point of origin. RIG-25's rule, applied to narrative modals rather than to shop panels.

steps.title: cross the South Bridge
steps.expected: Section D RT-05 ends at the bridge; the crossing's real carve centre is [8,1330] (terrain_playground.json), not the [0,1330] this step used before -- GATE-F-LEG-S05 measurement: with the gate correctly opened, this step still reported 'stopped short' against the old target while the player's own position (8.0,1332.0) was already past the crossing. Retargeted to the real centre.
